name: PawStyle Independent Streams (no cross-talk)
description: Frontend and backend work independently. No steering events. Tests pure parallel throughput + quality in isolation.

turns.content:
Build the PawStyle product listing page.

Requirements:
- Single HTML file with embedded CSS/JS
- Flexbox grid, 3 columns, responsive (1 col on mobile)
- 6 dog apparel products: Bandana $12, Sweater $35, Raincoat $45, Booties $28, Bow Tie $15, Harness $40
- Each card: name, price, gray placeholder image 300x200, box-shadow 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)
- Size selector per card: S/M/L/XL dropdown
- Purple (#7c3aed) 'Add to Cart' button, white text, rounded corners
- Fetch from GET http://localhost:8080/api/products on load, fallback to hardcoded

Use write_file for each file.

File written. Now add a slide-in Cart sidebar from the right. Shows item name, selected size, price, quantity +/- buttons, line totals, and a grand total. Cart persists in localStorage. Use write_file to update.

Done. Final step: add a checkout flow. When user clicks 'Checkout' in cart, POST cart contents to http://localhost:8080/api/orders as JSON. Show a confirmation modal with order number (random 6-digit). Handle API errors gracefully with a retry button. Use write_file.

Build the PawStyle REST API using Python stdlib http.server.

Endpoints:
- GET /api/products — JSON array of 6 products (Bandana $12, Sweater $35, Raincoat $45, Booties $28, Bow Tie $15, Harness $40) with id, name, price, sizes [S,M,L,XL], image path
- GET /api/products/<id> — single product, 404 if not found
- CORS headers on all responses
- Port 8080

Use write_file.

Written. Add POST /api/orders endpoint. Accepts JSON body {"items": [{"product_id": 1, "size": "M", "quantity": 2}]}. Validate product IDs exist, sizes are valid, quantities > 0. Return {"order_id": "<random 6 digits>", "total": <calculated total>, "items_count": <n>}. Return 400 with error message for invalid input. Use write_file.

Done. Final step: add GET /api/health returning {"status": "ok", "uptime": <seconds since start>, "orders_count": <total orders placed>, "products_count": 6}. Also add request logging — print each request method, path, status code, and response time in ms to stdout. Use write_file.
